source.title: Does the Model Use the Feature? Separating Steering from Mechanism in LLMs

page_placements.theme: Asymmetry between inducing and removing refusal

record.tranche_reason: The study directly intervenes on an Arditi-style refusal direction and measures instruction refusal, but fits the direction from answer-versus-refuse prompts rather than harmful-versus-harmless instructions.
record.gate_note: The refusal-direction control in Sections 5.2 and 5.4 bears on V1. The entity-latent and dense-direction results concern knowledge abstention, which the text distinguishes from safety and instruction refusal, so they are not recorded as V1 results. Cited results from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The refusal direction is only a positive control for the authors' interchange method. It is fit from prompts differing in an instruction to answer or refuse, not from harmful versus harmless instructions. Its measure is instructed refusal scored by a Qwen judge, not refusal of harmful requests. So the study induces refusal by instruction and checks that its own tests detect an effect. It does not test whether a harmful-minus-harmless direction mediates refusal. The main results concern knowledge abstention, which the authors say differs from safety and instruction refusal.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase covers only the refusal positive control. The authors' main conclusion is broader. Tracking a concept and steering a behaviour do not show the model uses a feature. The published entity latents steer knowledge abstention only beyond their natural range and transfer little of the natural contrast under interchange. Dense known–unknown directions dissociate installation from removal in Llama and Gemma. Feature claims must specify representation, site, edited tokens, update rule and measure. The refusal control illustrates that edited tokens matter.
record.recipe_differences: The refusal control uses a direction fit from paired answer-versus-refuse instructions, not the harmful-minus-harmless contrast. It tests a refusal-class-mean projection edit and compares one-site edits with all-layer, all-position directional ablation on Gemma 2 2B-IT.
record.method_sensitivity: The refusal change depends on intervention scope: removal at one site and token has a much smaller effect than ablation at all layers and positions.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma 2 2B-IT, a direction fit from answer-vs-refuse instructions installs instructed refusal at one token at a natural value (+29.0 pp). Removal at that site lowers it only 5–6 pp, while ablation at every layer and position lowers it 45 pp.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An instruction-refusal direction is sufficient at one site at natural values, but removing it requires intervention across layers and positions; conclusions depend on the edited tokens.

record.code_released: not stated (the complete experimental codebase is promised upon publication)
record.problems: The refusal control uses 100 prompts and does not report baseline or post-intervention refusal rates, so the remaining refusal after global ablation cannot be determined. It uses answer-versus-refuse prompts rather than testing refusal of harmful requests. General capability retention is not evaluated.

untested.parts: Harmful-minus-harmless direction; refusal of harmful requests; ablation removing and addition inducing such refusal; capability retention.
All (no weight edits on released models).

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T2/tests call is downgraded. The refusal direction is 'Arditi-style' only in its difference-in-means recipe. Its contrast (answer vs refuse instruction) and behaviour (instructed refusal) are not V1's harmful-request refusal, and it serves only to validate the authors' method. Baseline and post-intervention refusal rates are not reported, and capability retention is not measured.

versions.untested_parts: The refusal control does not test the harmful-minus-harmless direction recipe or refusal of harmful requests specifically; it does not report whether general capabilities remain intact.
Whether attacks suppress the direction or training against its ablation adds robustness.
Whether refusal is better described by an affine structure, cone, or multiple directions.
Whether harmfulness judgment is encoded separately from the refusal decision.
Transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
How refusal training choices determine whether a removable direction exists.

relation.reason: An Arditi-style direction is used as a positive control on a different construct (instructed refusal). No result bears on harmful-minus-harmless refusal mediation.

tranche.reason: The refusal direction serves only as a positive control for the authors' interchange tests. It is fit from answer-vs-refuse instruction pairs, and the measure is instructed refusal, which the text distinguishes from harmful-request refusal (line 217). It uses the finding as a tool and does not test any version.

source_check.notes: Absolute refusal rates (baseline and post-edit) are never reported; all four values are paired changes in pp from a Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct judge on 100 prompts. r1's op label 'addition' is really a class-mean projection set (r' = r + (q* - v^T r)v/||v||^2), not adding the direction.
